parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national binary sex/document rules plus division removal and school birth-certificate rule create traveler-facing entry, facility, care, and custody exposure. If outed, likely visa scrutiny/refusal, service/facility denial, and possible trespass arrest; if detained, severe abuse is documented. Minor/family travel worsens: care bans, school outing, records subpoenas. Rule-of-law protections in some states mitigate somewhat but do not offset operative restrictions. No execution or likely imprisonment for mere status, but tier-1 exposure puts this in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas enforce binary birth-sex marker; new X markers barred; discrepancies trigger refusal, additional evidence, possible fraud/permanent bar; reported confiscation/stranding; airport secondary screening can out.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; court challenges/legal-aid guidance; some states still permit marker changes, but these do not offset federal traveler screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch feeds border screening, visa denial, possible detention/investigation; state school/birth rules echo national sex definition.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; national prisons adopted conversion-style measures; facility-trespass arrest can mean men’s-ward detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime and constitutional avenues; litigation injunctions; no documented safe placement protocol; recourse uncertain.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancies or facility refusal can escalate into custody; hostile binary-sex rules shape placement and care denial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars congruent single-sex facilities; division school rule requires birth-certificate facilities for everyone on school grounds, including visitors; other states criminalize some facility use after refusal; state removed protections.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Other states have no bans or anti-discrimination law; map uncertainty; protections are not operative in division/school settings.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National rules plus state preemption create uneven but binding exposure at airports, government sites, and schools.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in division and many states; executive orders label care mutilation, freeze funding, threaten provider liability, and enable records subpoenas; crisis services cut; continuity may be denied.
care_services.protection: Adult coverage litigation and some state rules are climate signals, not documented traveler-facing mitigation; effectiveness uncertain.
care_services.interaction: Family/minor care needs interact with school grounds, national documents, provider chill, and funding bars; adult medication care is not clearly documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names “radically pro-transgender” groups as violent/hostile; reward system targets domestic terrorism; orders direct investigation of schools promoting gender identity; public opinion favors binary documents/athletics.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law; some state bias statutes; courts have blocked or enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing can justify scrutiny, denial, weak victim response, and chilling effects, though it is not a documented universal raid regime.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors on school grounds face birth-certificate restroom rules; guardian-consent alternatives are student-specific; care bans, school investigations, and records subpoenas can deny care/education and force outing.
minors_guardians.protection: Parentage, adoption, and marriage-related rulings are resident climate signals, not traveler-facing mitigation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel to schools/clinics raises forced outing, provider refusal, and possible guardian scrutiny; adult alone may avoid some encounters.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific documented trans violence rate; removed civil-rights coverage and hostile legal posture may encourage private harassment; police response is uncertain.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; 23 states have bias laws; 22 states plus capital district protect against discrimination, but enforcement varies.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence data are undercounts and cannot establish safety; legal hostility weakens remedy where service denial or assault occurs.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division preempts stronger local protections; no state remedy for gender-identity service denial; visa fraud waivers limited; several court cases unresolved; enforcement varies by state and time.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQs, some injunctions, and existing valid X passports may help; courts sometimes intervene.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown which orders are live at travel time; partial rule-of-law mediates but does not cancel operative federal/state restrictions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Above 0.25-A because there is no documented weekly raid pattern against venues, but similar: birth-sex document rules, hostile facilities policy, and severe custody consequences keep it in High Risk.

Below 0.45-A: it lacks a linked biometric daily registry, but visa/fraud exposure, school birth-certificate rules, criminal facility risk, and documented custody abuse make consequences harsher than ordinary administrative friction.

Materially below 0.85-A: protections are contested and removed in the division, local remedies are preempted, federal documents/facilities restrict access, and custody/care hostility is documented; equality machinery is not uniformly operative.

Far above 0.15-A: no credible routine long pretrial custody, coerced confessions, or capital threat for mere presentation; severe harm is conditional on detention/visa/facility encounters rather than automatic discovery-to-prison.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime layers federal document/entry restrictions with state-level hostility: border screening can refuse or strand applicants and create fraud exposure; school and government facilities enforce birth-certificate placement; care for minors and school speech are criminalized; custody amplifies severity with documented abuse. Adult travelers may avoid some sites, but any checkpoint, school event, emergency, or arrest exposes them. Family/minor travel intensifies care denial, outing, and guardian scrutiny. Legal protections and court variability provide partial mitigation, yet absent effective remedy in the division and federal enforcement lower this into High Risk.
